paths.title: Collaborative Branch Workflow
paths.description: Keep branches focused, current, reviewable, and safe to integrate.
concept: A branch is a movable reference to commits
Branches make parallel work possible, but integration quality depends on clear ownership and coherent changes.
A good branch tells one story, avoids unrelated churn, and can be validated independently.
workflow: Prepare a reviewable branch
Reduce integration risk before opening the pull request.
Review should focus on intent and behavior rather than avoidable repository noise.
Start from the current target branch.
Create a descriptive branch.
Make focused commits.
Run repository checks frequently.
Fetch target-branch updates.
Resolve conflicts by preserving both intentions.
Review the final diff.
Push and open a draft pull request.
question: Keep a pull request focused
Which change most improves review quality?
Mixing a refactor, feature, and formatting sweep
Separating unrelated changes into distinct pull requests
Hiding generated files among source edits
Skipping the final diff
Focused pull requests reduce cognitive load, make rollback easier, and help reviewers evaluate one intention.
checklist: Branch integration checklist
Confirm that the branch is safe to review and merge.
The final branch state matters more than whether each individual commit once passed.
The branch targets the intended base.
The diff contains no unrelated edits.
Generated artifacts are intentional.
Conflicts were resolved semantically.
Tests pass on the final head.
Commit messages explain purpose.
The pull request documents risks and limitations.

paths.title: History Repair and Recovery
paths.description: Use revert, reset, restore, reflog, rebase, and cherry-pick without losing work.
concept: Published history should usually be repaired additively
A revert creates a new commit that undoes an earlier change while preserving shared history.
Reset and force-push rewrite references and are safer on private work than shared branches.
workflow: Recover from a mistaken change
Choose the least destructive operation that matches the repository state.
Inspect the working tree, index, branch, and publication status before acting.
Stop and inspect status and recent commits.
Save uncommitted work if necessary.
Determine whether the bad change is published.
Use restore for selected file content.
Use revert for shared commits.
Use reset only with clear intent.
Use reflog to locate moved references.
Verify the recovered diff before pushing.
question: Undo a merged shared commit
Which operation is normally safest for undoing a commit already merged to a shared main branch?
Delete the repository
Create a revert commit
Force-push main to an older commit
Remove the remote
Revert preserves published history and creates an explicit, reviewable inverse change.
checklist: Destructive Git command review
Pause before operations that can discard or rewrite work.
A short inspection often prevents hours of recovery.
The current branch is confirmed.
Uncommitted changes are understood.
The target commit or path is exact.
Publication and collaborators are considered.
A backup branch or reflog path exists.
Force-with-lease is preferred when rewriting is necessary.
The result is inspected immediately.

paths.title: Repository Governance and Automation
paths.description: Use protections, ownership, status checks, releases, and dependency controls to maintain quality.
concept: Branch protections and required checks turn expected engineering practice into consistent merge rules.
Policies should target meaningful risks without becoming so slow that contributors bypass them.
workflow: Define a protected integration path
Make important branches change only through reviewed, validated work.
Rules should identify who can approve, which checks are required, and how emergencies are handled.
Identify protected branches.
Require pull requests for changes.
Require relevant status checks.
Set review and ownership rules.
Restrict force pushes and deletion.
Define release or provenance requirements.
Document emergency bypass and audit it.
question: Choose a meaningful required check
Which check is most appropriate to require before merging application code?
A test and validation workflow covering the changed behavior
A random delay
A decorative label only
A check that always reports success
Required checks should provide evidence about correctness, security, or deployability of the exact commit.
checklist: Repository governance review
Confirm that automation protects quality without hiding ownership.
Automation should make decisions visible and leave a trace for releases and incidents.
Protected branches reject unsafe updates.
Review rules match real expertise.
Required checks run on the merge candidate.
Dependencies and secrets are scanned.
Release tags and artifacts are traceable.
Permissions are reviewed periodically.
Bypasses and failed checks are auditable.
